text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed two Xid 13 / ECC warnings on a p4 node in us-west1 around 06:11 UTC. dmesg had long noise so I grabbed a tail. Thinking we should standardize a small dmesg/journalctl/nvidia-smi snapshot for faster triage.

kevin: Can you paste the minimal grep you used? if we add a fast collector we should keep payload <= 200KB to avoid costing S3/ingest. :money_with_wings:

maria: sure, this is what I ran locally:
```bash
dmesg | egrep -i 'Xid|Ecc|NVRM' -A4 || true
sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-persistenced --since "15 minutes ago" | tail -n 200
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid,utilization.gpu,memory.used,driver_version --format=csv
```

kevin: perfect. sample output snippet I saw in the node: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=25678, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.567915] NVRM: Ecc error count increased on GPU 0
```

sam: quick thought — we already have full dmesg shipping for node snapshots but it's too big for hot triage. propose a new "mini-snapshot" that includes: last 500 dmesg lines filtered for keywords, last 200 journalctl lines for nvidia-related units, and a single nvidia-smi CSV plus top-level pod/container ownership. keeps size small and consistent.

anya: +1. Also add node labels (nodepool, zone, kernel-version) and the list of recent reboots from systemd (last -n 5 -x). Those fields made a big difference last time.

logship-bot: FYI: current loghook policy (v2) caps system logs at 1MB per upload and drops binary blobs. Changing schema requires migration.

maria: here's a proposed manifest for the mini-snapshot (keeps fields explicit):
```json
{
  "collect": [
    "dmesg.tail:500:filter=Xid,Ecc,NVRM",
    "journalctl.unit:nvidia-persistenced:lines=200",
    "nvidia-smi:csv",
    "container-map:pods-on-gpus"
  ],
  "labels": ["node","zone","nodepool","kernel_version","reboothistory"]
}
```

kevin: that looks good. for parsing we should add a regex extractor for Xid patterns and ECC counters so we can auto-classify failures into categories: ECC-increment, Xid-13-falloff, driver-crash, thermal. will add rule to loghook: `XID_RE = /Xid \(.*\): (\d+)/`

sam: also want a small heuristic: if Xid 13 appears with "GPU has fallen off the bus" and there are nvlink resets in the last 60s, mark node as candidate for immediate drain. Otherwise keep metrics-only alert and follow up.

anya: we should avoid auto-drain unless >2 distinct GPUs hit the same pattern in 1h to reduce flapping. propose thresholds in runbook.

maria: action items: 1) kevin to add Xid/ECC extractors to loghook and index schema (ETA: 24h). 2) sam to add mini-snapshot CLI + runbook snippet (ETA: 2d). 3) infra-eng to file a quick deploy plan to roll this to logship-bot config with staged rollout (canary on staging gpupool).

kevin: start a PR for extractor and a mapping doc. will ping when ready.

sam: I'll draft the CLI command and an example `collect-mini-snapshot.sh` that ops can run during oncall. snippet: 
```bash
#!/bin/bash
NODE=$1
ssh $NODE <<'SSH'
dmesg | egrep -i 'Xid|Ecc|NVRM' -A6 | tail -n 500
sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-persistenced --since "30 minutes ago" | tail -n 200
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid,utilization.gpu,memory.used,driver_version --format=csv
kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=$(hostname) -o wide
SSH
```

oncall-bot: @maria noted — oncall escalation: if mini-snapshot shows Xid 13 + ECC increment on same GPU, page infra-sre.

maria: also thinking about long-term: we should start storing an aggregated counter per GPU (daily ECC increments, Xid counts) in metrics to detect slowly degrading cards. might be part of Optimize later.

kevin: agreed. will add metric names: `gpu.ecc.errors.delta` and `gpu.xid.count` to the telemetry backlog.

anya: can we also include a short example of correlating with pod logs? a quick `kubectl logs` snippet in the runbook so app owners can see who was running when the failure hit.

sam: added to runbook draft. final Q: where do we put the mini-snapshots? a separate bucket path `redwood-gpu-mini-snapshots/{zone}/{node}/{ts}` so we can keep retention shorter.

maria: agree on bucket layout. logship-bot — can you accept config change once we have PRs?

logship-bot: I can. create PR against `infra/logship/config/v3` and add `mini-snapshot` collector. will enforce size limit 400KB and gzip.

kevin: thanks — I'll open extractor PR in the next 2 hours.

sam: I'll push runbook and example script later today.

anya: thanks team. this should shave ~15min off triage for flaky cards. :tada:

infra-eng: noted for sprint planning — add follow-up ticket to implement metrics aggregation and the 2-week rollout plan.
